headline: Biggest liquidity cushion and cheapest multiple of the big three, but weak Q4 guidance shows fuel can still swamp record revenue.
business: Largest U.S. airline by revenue ($65.6B TTM), with seven U.S. hubs including Newark, Chicago, Denver, Houston and San Francisco, and the deepest Pacific and Atlantic network. Premium cabins and MileagePlus drive margin.
recent: Q3 2026 revenue was a record $17.9B (+17.4% YoY) on higher yields; GAAP net income $1.03B, adjusted EPS $2.54 (-8.6%).
Fuel expense rose 61.6% to $4.84B as the average price hit $3.90/gal vs $2.43 a year earlier, with gallons roughly flat.
Q4 revenue growth guided above 20%, but per Skift, Q4 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.50-$1.50 (at $4.80/gal fuel) sits well below the $1.76 consensus.
strengths: Highest ROE in the group (22%) and #2 net margin
$17.7B of available liquidity, the largest cushion of the peers
Pricing power: Q4 revenue expected up more than 20%
risks: $26.4B of debt and finance leases; free cash flow negative (-$0.6B TTM)
Highly exposed to jet fuel staying near $4.80/gal
International demand sensitive to the Middle East conflict
catalysts: Q4 2026 results and 2027 guide in January
Any easing in crude/jet fuel prices
Continued premium and loyalty revenue growth
